32383-two-wyoming-girls-and-their-homest.title: A Story for Girls
32383-two-wyoming-girls-and-their-homest.creator: Unknown
32383-two-wyoming-girls-and-their-homest.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. "Going to work in the mines!" Jessie echoed the words, as, I am sure, I did also. I was sitting in the corner dressing little Ralph, or, to be strictly accurate, trying to dress him. No three year-old that ever lived could be more exasperating than he sometimes was during that ordeal or could show a more pronounced distaste for the bondage of civilized garments.

arxiv-2203-11576.title: Predictor Selection for Synthetic Controls
arxiv-2203-11576.creator: Jaume Vives-i-Bastida
arxiv-2203-11576.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jaume Vives-i-Bastida. Synthetic control methods often rely on matching pre-treatment characteristics (called predictors) of the treated unit. The choice of predictors and how they are weighted plays a key role in the performance and interpretability of synthetic control estimators. This paper proposes the use of a sparse synthetic control procedure that penalizes the number of predictors used in generating the counterfactual to select the most important predictors.

arxiv-2303-04737.title: SoftMatch Distance: A Novel Distance for Weakly-Supervised Trend Change Detection in Bi-Temporal Images
arxiv-2303-04737.creator: Yuqun Yang, Xu Tang, Xiangrong Zhang, Jingjing Ma, Licheng Jiao
arxiv-2303-04737.description: Abstract General change detection (GCD) and semantic change detection (SCD) are common methods for identifying changes and distinguishing object categories involved in those changes, respectively. However, the binary changes provided by GCD is often not practical enough, while annotating semantic labels for training SCD models is very expensive.

arxiv-2306-07526.title: User-defined Event Sampling and Uncertainty Quantification in Diffusion Models for Physical Dynamical Systems
arxiv-2306-07526.creator: Marc Finzi, Anudhyan Boral, Andrew Gordon Wilson, Fei Sha, Leonardo Zepeda-Núñez
arxiv-2306-07526.description: Abstract Diffusion models are a class of probabilistic generative models that have been widely used as a prior for image processing tasks like text conditional generation and inpainting. We demonstrate that these models can be adapted to make predictions and provide uncertainty quantification for chaotic dynamical systems.

arxiv-2404-05569.title: 360 ∘ 360^{\circ} REA: Towards A Reusable Experience Accumulation with 360 ∘ 360^{\circ} Assessment for Multi-Agent System
arxiv-2404-05569.creator: Shen Gao, Hao Li, Chengrui Huang, Quan Tu, Zhiliang Tian * , Minlie Huang, Shuo Shang
arxiv-2404-05569.description: Abstract Large language model agents have demonstrated remarkable advancements across various complex tasks. Recent works focus on optimizing the agent team or employing self-reflection to iteratively solve complex tasks. Since these agents are all based on the same LLM, only conducting self-evaluation or removing underperforming agents does not substantively enhance the capability of the agents.

arxiv-2407-16078.title: Parametric Representations of Neutron-Star Equations of State With Phase Transitions
arxiv-2407-16078.creator: Lee Lindblom
arxiv-2407-16078.description: Abstract This paper explores the use of low-dimensional parametric representations of neutron-star equations of state that include discontinuities caused by phase transitions. The accuracies of optimal piecewise-analytic and spectral representations are evaluated for equations of state having first- or second-order phase transitions with a wide range of discontinuity sizes.

Illingworth’s research was supported by
arxiv-2410-18281.creator: Alberto Espuny Díaz, Emma Hogan, Freddie Illingworth, Lukas Michel, Julien Portier, Jun Yan
arxiv-2410-18281.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alberto Espuny Díaz, Emma Hogan, Freddie Illingworth, Lukas Michel, Julien Portier, Jun Yan. We construct a set of 2 n 2^{n} points in ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} such that all pairwise Manhattan distances are odd integers, which improves the recent linear lower bound of Golovanov, Kupavskii and Sagdeev. In contrast to the Euclidean and maximum metrics, this shows that the odd-distance set problem behaves very differently to the equilateral set problem under the Manhattan metric.

pmc-11669018.title: A Case of Arterial Bypass for Extensive Stenosis of the Ulnar Artery and Superficial Palmar Arch due to Hypothenar Hammer Syndrome
pmc-11669018.creator: Fumikazu Tamura, Kaoru Sasaki, Junya Oshima, Yoichiro Shibuya, Masahiro Sasaki, Yukiko Aihara, Mitsuru Sekido
pmc-11669018.description: We present a case of arterial bypass for extensive stenosis of the ulnar artery and superficial palmar arch. The ulnar artery and the superficial palmar arch were bypassed using the great saphenous vein. Postoperatively, blood flow to the affected fingers gradually improved and the pain disappeared.

pmc-11714307.title: Prognostic value of a novel plasma pTau217 assay for amyloid accumulation in healthy elderly
pmc-11714307.creator: Steffi De Meyer, Emma S. Luckett, Jolien Schaeverbeke, Koen Van Laere, Jeroen Vanbrabant, Eugeen Vanmechelen, Patrick Dupont, Guglielmo Di Molfetta, Henrik Zetterberg, Nicholas J. Ashton, Koen Poesen, Rik Vandenberghe
pmc-11714307.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe performance of blood‐based phosphorylated tau (pTau) immunoassays to detect asymptomatic Alzheimer’s disease (AD) has important implications for therapeutic trials. pTau217 is often recommended as the preferred epitope due to its high fold changes in AD.

pmc-12724093.title: Confirmatory factor analysis of competing PANSS negative symptom models: data from OPTiMiSE first-episode schizophrenia study
pmc-12724093.creator: Arsime Demjaha, Daniel Stahl, Celso Arango, Birte Glenthøj, Roberto Rodriguez-Jimenez, Covadonga Martinez Díaz-Caneja, Lone Baandrup, Bjørn Ebdrup, Maria Paz Garcia-Portlla, Maria Diaz-Marsa, Inge Winter-van Rossum, Rene Kahn, Paola Dazzan, Philip McGuire
pmc-12724093.description: BackgroundThe negative symptoms of psychosis are heterogeneous, which complicates efforts to understand their pathophysiology and develop effective treatments. Factor analytic studies of the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) have reported two factorial negative symptom models, expressive deficit and social amotivation, albeit with different compositions.

pmc-13083098.title: Exploring the mechanism of Yin Huo decoction in PCPA-induced depression mice: a metabolomics and network pharmacology approach
pmc-13083098.creator: Yu Zhou, Lu Jia Liu, Yue Zhang, Wen Wen Wang, Dan Hong Xu
pmc-13083098.description: IntroductionDepression is a prevalent neuropsychiatric disorder, and traditional Chinese medicine formulations such as Yin Huo Decoction (YHD) have shown potential antidepressant effects, yet their underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of YHD in a PCPA-induced depression model in mice.

pmc-13087285.title: Method comparison of microscopy, metabarcoding, and multispectral imaging flow cytometry for identification and relative abundance analysis of insect-dispersed pollen
pmc-13087285.creator: Elena Motivans Švara, Demetra Rakosy, Tiffany M Knight, Alexander Keller, Thomas Hornick, Franziska Walther, Susanne Dunker
pmc-13087285.description: Pollen identification and quantification are essential in ecological and evolutionary research to address plant-pollinator relationships, pollination services, and plant reproduction. Research into pollen transfer patterns has been mainly based on traditional light microscopy, however, it is time consuming, labour intensive, and requires taxonomic expertise. High-throughput methods allow automated pollen identification across large temporal and spatial scales.

pmc-13496041.title: Ratiometric Mycotoxin Detection in Living Plants With Dual‐Emissive Nanosensors
pmc-13496041.creator: Yuliang Li, Di Shen, Ziyang Huang, Suppanat Puangpathumanond, Calvin Thenarianto, Yue Zhao, Jolly Madathiparambil Saju, Rajani Sarojam, Dongmei Zhou, Tedrick Thomas Salim Lew
pmc-13496041.description: Early diagnosis of fungal infections in crops is essential for mitigating yield losses, yet most detection strategies rely on destructive assays that are incompatible with in situ monitoring.
